clue.text: This castle's situated far south of the city

definitions.text: This castle's situated far south of the city

parts.words: This castle's situated far south of the city
parts.note: a castle in Kent shares its name with a big Yorkshire city hundreds of miles to the north, so the castle and the city carry one name

explanation.surface: A guidebook note placing a castle well away from the town it shares a name with.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds Castle is in Kent, in the south-east of England, while the city of Leeds is in Yorkshire in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes a famous Kentish castle by its odd location relative to its northern namesake city.

clue.text: Unusual ideas in wedding round the altar, unconventionally

indicators.note: round means the joining word is placed around the other letters

parts.note: wedding is joining, so linking

indicators.note: unconventionally says the words the altar are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Odd notions about a couple circling the altar during an unusual wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wedding' looks like part of the scene at the altar, but it is the joining word; 'unconventionally' rearranges THE ALTAR to ATERALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking in an indirect, creative way produces unexpected, unusual ideas.

clue.text: Command from censor to suppress chapter

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down or keep in, so the censoring word holds the chapter letter inside

parts.note: to censor a text is to edit it

explanation.surface: An order from the censor that a chapter be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An official decree is an authoritative command.

clue.text: Return to cover second round of contest male entered

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round of a race or contest
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A sporting report on a man entering the second round of a competition and going back to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' only joins: the male pronoun is entered after the round.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a sword back into its scabbard is to return it to its cover.

clue.text: Maestro in action's totally transformed

indicators.note: totally transformed says the letters of the words in action's are wholly rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor who becomes a different man once he is in action.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'action's' is part of the fodder: IN ACTIONS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor, a classic maestro.

clue.text: Skirt you repeatedly found abroad

indicators.note: repeatedly says the foreign word for you appears twice in a row

parts.note: tu is French for you, signalled by 'found abroad'

explanation.surface: A remark that you keep coming across a certain skirt overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found abroad' tells you to use a foreign word: French TU.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by ballet dancers.

clue.text: Swan can, when trapped in dry lake

indicators.note: trapped in says the swan and can letters sit within the word for dry

parts.note: sere means dry or withered
a pen is a female swan
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A swan and a tin can stuck in a lake that has dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is the lake in Hyde Park, London, known for its swans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serpentine is a well-known ornamental body of water in a London park.

clue.text: It throws light on a right fix

parts.note: to clamp is to fix firmly in place

explanation.surface: Something that illuminates a correct repair job.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of electric lamp produces intense illumination from a spark between electrodes.

clue.text: Ancient herbivore providing one with manure to put on

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
guano is bird droppings used as manure
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Gardening advice about fertilising with manure that you put on the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant-eating dinosaur was one of the first to be identified from fossils.

clue.text: Almost home from touring holiday, meeting emergency

definitions.meaning: read literally: on a tour, the final stop before home is the last place you stay
dealing with a crisis, when every other option is gone

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means 'as a final option', but here also its literal sense: at the final holiday town of a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means when nothing else is left, as in a crisis; literally it is the final place visited.

clue.text: Get rid of some fat in period at university

parts.note: to trim is to cut away excess, getting rid of some
fats are esters, chemically, so an ester stands for some fat

explanation.surface: A student resolving to lose a little weight during a term at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is one of three divisions of an academic year at some universities.

clue.text: Piece of bread and wine offered by holy person

parts.note: a cru is a wine of a particular vineyard or grade
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Bread and wine handed out by a saint, as at a communion.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust is a hard end or broken piece of a loaf.

clue.text: Run out to gallery to copy Turner?

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An art student dashing off to the Tate to copy a J. M. W. Turner painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, whose work is in the Tate, but a turner is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin round is to imitate something that turns, a turner, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Prisoner, French collaborator, executed and thrown in river

indicators.note: thrown in says the shortened name is dropped inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: executed here means beheaded, so the collaborator loses his first letter

parts.note: Marshal Petain headed the Vichy regime that collaborated with Nazi Germany

explanation.surface: A wartime traitor being shot and his body tossed into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Petain led Vichy France; 'executed' is read as beheaded, leaving ETAIN, though Petain was in fact reprieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in custody is a prisoner.

clue.text: Lookalike shot in place of chief criminal

indicators.note: in place says the shot word is set inside the lookalike word

parts.note: a ringer is someone who looks just like another, a dead ringer
lead is the metal of shot fired from a gun

explanation.surface: A double gunned down instead of the gang boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a gang of wrongdoers is the one who leads them.

clue.text: Damage to car lets in criminal

indicators.note: damage to these words breaks them up and rebuilds them in a different order

explanation.surface: A vandal damages a car and so admits being a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits theft is a thief, a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Annoyed, relaxing, to. be interrupted by opponents at table

indicators.note: interrupted by says the opponents' letters break into the middle of the relaxing word

parts.note: restful means relaxing
at the bridge table East and North are opponents, E and N

explanation.surface: A bridge player annoyed that a relaxing game is interrupted by the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'to' is a print slip and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling bitter and aggrieved is a way of being annoyed.

clue.text: They support maestri, and help opera with backing

indicators.note: with backing says the help and opera letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: aid means help
OP is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work, used here for opera

explanation.surface: Patrons who support conductors and help the opera with financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with backing' turns AID + OP into PODIA as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Conductors stand on raised platforms, which hold them up.

clue.text: Drove to a plant.

parts.note: a drove is a large crowd, a host

explanation.surface: Someone drove to a factory or garden centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are leafy shade-loving garden perennials.

clue.text: A good look round front of temple for goddess

indicators.note: round says the staring word goes around the first letter of temple

parts.note: a stare is a long hard look

indicators.note: front of means only the first letter of temple is used

explanation.surface: A visitor looks round the front of a temple dedicated to a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.

clue.text: Spicy snap of redhead?

definitions.meaning: a ginger head, nut being slang for head

explanation.walkthrough: A gingernut is a hard British ginger biscuit, and nut is slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a ginger-flavoured biscuit; read in two parts it is a red-haired head.

clue.text: Reflecting how parrot is talking

definitions.meaning: sending back sound, as a wall does
a parrot repeats what it hears

explanation.definitionFit: Repeating sound back describes both a reflecting surface and a mimicking parrot.

clue.text: Period just ended square, with level outcomes

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
ties are matches ending level

explanation.surface: A sports season that just finished all square, with many drawn results.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared at the turn of the century, so the 1990s had just ended.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade of the 1990s had just finished when this puzzle was set.

clue.text: A few words from actor finally entering stage

indicators.note: entering says that last letter goes inside the word for stage

parts.note: a phase is a stage of development

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of actor is taken

explanation.surface: An actor finally coming on stage to deliver a few lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A short group of words is a phrase.

clue.text: Fit to take on king in dispute

indicators.note: to take on is to take in or admit, so the fit holds the king letter

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Someone fit to take on the king in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute a point.

clue.text: Jazz technique taken up by Duke

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: art means skill or technique

explanation.surface: Duke Ellington adopting a new jazz technique.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD is traditional jazz; the surface invites Duke Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the New Orleans style.

clue.text: Conclude fine combination aimed at king

indicators.note: a combination of the letters of fine puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A chess player decides a neat combination of moves is aimed at the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce or reach a conclusion from evidence is to conclude.

clue.text: Heroic action going wrong in curious setback

indicators.note: in says the going-wrong word sits inside the reversed word
setback means the word for curious is set back to front

parts.note: odd means curious or strange
erring means going wrong

explanation.surface: A bold deed that goes awry in a strange reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' gives DDO from the word for curious; the surface reads as a single bad reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring, heroic action.

clue.text: Plant or cane

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold, so golden
a rod is a cane or stick

explanation.surface: A choice between a plant and a cane, as in staking the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but is heraldry's gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall plant with yellow flower spikes.

clue.text: Pregnant, so some are born?

definitions.meaning: an old sense: carrying a child, as in 'with child'
Shakespeare's Twelfth Night: some are born to greatness, some achieve it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Some are born great' is from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; 'great with child' means pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heavy with child is an old sense of the word, and Malvolio's letter says some are born with greatness.
